extracted.intended_audience: Title IX coordinators, school administrators, legal/compliance staff, and educational institutions (elementary, secondary, and postsecondary) that receive Federal financial assistance
extracted.subtask_description: Final Department of Education regulations (34 CFR 106) specifying legally binding obligations for recipients of federal education funds to prevent, respond to, investigate, adjudicate, and remedy sexual harassment and related Title IX issues. The document lays out definitions, grievance-process requirements, procedural protections, and enforcement/recordkeeping obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Sexual Harassment (§106.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sexual harassment is defined by three prongs: (1) quid pro quo; (2) hostile environment under Davis standard (so severe and pervasive, objectively offensive, and effectively denies equal access); and (3) sexual assault, dating violence, domestic violence, or stalking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explains support and opposition for each prong, subdivides the Davis standard into its components (so severe and pervasive; objectively offensive; effectively denies equal access), and treats prong (3) as explicit enumerated acts. The regulation discusses application across elementary/secondary and postsecondary contexts and addresses gender‑based harassment and related terminology concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual Knowledge (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient has 'actual knowledge' of sexual harassment when an official with authority to institute corrective measures has notice of harassment, which triggers obligations to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule discusses who counts as an official, concerns about burdening complainants, confusion for employees, intersections with deliberate indifference, and jurisdictional limits such as 'education program or activity' and 'against a person in the U.S.' including issues for study abroad and online harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate Indifference Standard (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's response to known sexual harassment must not be 'deliberately indifferent' — i.e., it must be responsive enough to eliminate the harassment, prevent its recurrence, and remedy its effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble addresses how deliberate indifference is applied, recipient self-interest vs. burdening complainants, intersection with IDEA/Section 504/ADA, requests for clarifications, and how OCR will enforce the provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive Measures (§106.44 / §106.30 definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures promptly to persons alleged to be victimized by sexual harassment; supportive measures may be available to either party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble discusses examples (e.g., no-contact orders), overall support and opposition, safe harbor proposals that were removed, and clarification requests about the scope and listing of supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency Removal (§106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may implement emergency removal of a respondent when an individualized safety and risk analysis supports removal, while providing notice and an opportunity to challenge the removal immediately following it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is discussion of support and opposition, intersection with special education laws (IDEA/504/ADA), post-removal challenges, absence of stated time limits, definitions of 'removal', and OCR enforcement expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Leave (§106.44(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may place an employee respondent on administrative leave consistent with applicable laws and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble discusses administrative leave generally along with concerns, applicability to employees, and interaction with other laws and employment practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Requirements for the §106.45 Grievance Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must resolve allegations promptly and accurately under a predictable, fair grievance process that provides due process protections to both complainants and respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble summarizes §106.45, explains its similarity/differences with prior Department guidance, and frames goals of prompt, supportive responses and effective remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable Treatment of Complainants and Respondents (§106.45(b)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide equitable treatment to both parties throughout the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments and concerns discussed include what equitable treatment means in practice and how to implement protections while respecting due process and survivor-oriented considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective Evaluation of All Relevant Evidence (§106.45(b)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers must objectively evaluate all relevant evidence, inculpatory and exculpatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble emphasizes avoiding bias, ensuring accuracy, and not weighing evidence in a one-sided manner; ties to training and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and Mandatory Training of Title IX Personnel (§106.45(b)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and other personnel must be impartial and receive mandatory, adequate training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directed Question 4 and related discussion address scope/content of training, conflicts of interest, impartiality standards, and ensuring personnel can evaluate questions of relevance and trauma-informed responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of Non-Responsibility (§106.45(b)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must presume the respondent not responsible at the outset of the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explains the purpose of the presumption, debates about dual presumption or no presumption, impacts on students of color/LGBTQ/individuals with disabilities, false allegations concerns, and implications for due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably Prompt Time Frames (§106.45(b)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must contain reasonably prompt time frames for major stages of the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments addressed support and opposition to unspecified time limits, effects on recipients, concurrent law enforcement activity, and requests for alternative proposals or clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe Range or List of Possible Sanctions and Remedies (§106.45(b)(1)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must describe the range of possible disciplinary sanctions and remedies that may be imposed following a determination of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble emphasizes use of the term 'disciplinary sanctions' consistently and discusses how remedies relate to eliminating effects of harassment and restoring equal access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe Standard of Evidence (§106.45(b)(1)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must state the standard of evidence the recipient uses to reach determinations regarding responsibility (e.g., preponderance of the evidence or higher).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document discusses debates over preponderance vs. clear-and-convincing, arguments for/against mandating a particular standard, safety/accuracy tradeoffs, and consistency across recipient types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and Bases for Appeal (§106.45(b)(1)(viii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide procedures and permitted bases for appeals in their grievance processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section requires equal opportunity to appeal for both parties on specified bases (e.g., procedural irregularity, new evidence, bias) and includes discussion of appeal mechanics and fairness concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe Range of Supportive Measures (§106.45(b)(1)(ix))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures should describe the supportive measures available to parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This overlaps with the supportive measures requirement; commenters sought clarity and examples; the final rule expects description of types of available measures and their implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privileged Information (§106.45(b)(1)(x))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must address how privileged information is treated and when it may be excluded from the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explains interactions with privilege rules, the need to inform parties, and limits on relying on privileged materials without appropriate procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Notice of Allegations (§106.45(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide written notice to the parties of the allegations, sufficient details to understand the allegations, and any known time/place behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussions include timing of notice, updates to notice as the investigation proceeds, and ensuring that notices enable meaningful opportunity to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning Against False Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must warn parties regarding making false statements in the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble highlights the need to guard against false statements while balancing concerns about chilling reporting and fairness to complainants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory and Discretionary Dismissal (§106.45(b)(3)(i)-(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must specify mandatory dismissal grounds (e.g., conduct not meeting Title IX sexual harassment definition or outside jurisdiction) and discretionary dismissal procedures with notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble details mandatory vs. discretionary dismissal, notice requirements, and consolidation of complaints where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of Formal Complaints (§106.45(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures must describe when formal complaints may be consolidated (e.g., allegations against multiple respondents or by multiple complainants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document discusses fairness, notice, and impacts on investigation logistics when consolidating matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burdens of Proof and Gathering Evidence Rest on the Recipient (§106.45(b)(5)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient bears the burden of proof and responsibility for gathering evidence during the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble clarifies that recipients must investigate actively rather than placing investigative burden solely on individual parties, and discusses resource/administrative burdens on schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal Opportunity to Present Witnesses and Evidence (§106.45(b)(5)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party must have an equal opportunity to present witnesses and inculpatory/exculpatory evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule addresses witness access, limitations to protect parties (e.g., rape shield), and balancing fairness with trauma-informed practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients Must Not Restrict Parties' Ability To Discuss Allegations (§106.45(b)(5)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should not restrict either party's ability to discuss allegations or to gather and present relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble stresses free discussion but also recognizes confidentiality concerns and union/confidentiality constraints on personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisors of Choice (§106.45(b)(5)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties have the right to have an advisor of their choice present during meetings, interviews, investigations, and hearings; advisors may conduct cross-examination in live hearings (for postsecondary institutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses supporting presence/participation of advisors, fairness considerations, conflicts of interest, confidentiality, union issues, and modifications (e.g., when advisors are unavailable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Notice of Hearings, Meetings, and Interviews (§106.45(b)(5)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide timely written notice of hearings, investigative interviews, and meetings to parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble outlines expectations for sufficient notice, scheduling, and opportunities to prepare; concerns about administrative burdens are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection and Review of Evidence Directly Related to the Allegations (§106.45(b)(5)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must be given the opportunity to inspect and review all evidence directly related to the allegations, including evidence the recipient does not intend to rely upon in its determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directed Question 7 and discussion emphasize transparency, time to respond, and limits tied to privilege or privacy protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative Report That Fairly Summarizes Relevant Evidence (§106.45(b)(5)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must prepare an investigative report that fairly summarizes relevant evidence and provide it to the parties before any determination or hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report must be provided with sufficient time for parties to review and prepare responses; commenters discussed accuracy, accountability, and how report drafting prevents biased outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings and Cross-Examination (§106.45(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: For postsecondary institutions, recipients must provide a live hearing at which cross‑examination is conducted by advisors; for elementary/secondary, written questions may be used. No decision may rely on statements of a party who does not submit to cross-examination at a live hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive discussion addresses support/opposition to cross-examination, retraumatization risk, demeanor unreliability, trauma responses, rape-shield protections, separate rooms/technology facilitation, financial inequities, and how to exclude abusive or irrelevant questions while preserving due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Reliance on Statements Not Subject to Cross-Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not rely on statements of a party or witness who does not submit to cross-examination at a live hearing in reaching a determination of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule is intended to ensure parties can test evidence; the preamble explains impacts on participation and how to balance with protections for trauma-impacted witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rape-Shield Protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures and hearings must include rape-shield protections limiting questions/ evidence about a complainant's sexual history irrelevant to the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble addresses scope of such protections and how they interact with cross-examination and relevance determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary and Secondary Hearing Modifications (§106.45(b)(6)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Elementary and secondary school recipients may use hearings without live cross-examination and must provide parties the opportunity to submit written questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation recognizes developmental and safety concerns for minors and allows adapted procedures for younger students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Investigator Model Prohibited (§106.45(b)(7)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The single-investigator model (where one person investigates, decides responsibility, and sanctions) is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explains rationale (avoiding concentration of roles that can produce bias), benefits of separation of roles, consistency with case law, and alternative approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinations Regarding Responsibility—Written Determination (§106.45(b)(7)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must issue a written determination regarding responsibility that includes specific required details (allegations, procedural steps, findings, rationale, sanctions/remedies, appeal rights, and when decision is final).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble highlights the purpose of required contents, transparency, and concurrent notification to parties; connections to prior guidance (e.g., 2001, 2011) are discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of When the Decision Becomes Final (§106.45(b)(7)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must specify when the written determination becomes final (including how appeals affect finality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble discusses timing, transcript notations, implementation of remedies, and effective dates for disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals (§106.45(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer both parties an equal opportunity to appeal a determination on listed bases (e.g., procedural irregularity, new evidence, bias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document discusses appeal scope, parity for parties, procedures, and how appeals interact with remedies and final determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal Resolution (§106.45(b)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may offer voluntary informal resolution options (e.g., mediation, restorative justice), but these must be voluntary, non-binding, and not required in sexual assault cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble notes support/concern for informal resolution, survivor-centered protections, confidentiality implications, voluntary consent, restorative justice approaches, and safeguards (written notice, ability to withdraw).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping (§106.45(b)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must maintain records of investigations, determinations, appeals, and supportive measures as required by the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directed Question 8 and discussion address retention periods, access by the Department, interactions with privacy laws (FERPA), and disclosure obligations during Department investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Title IX Coordinator (§106.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each recipient must designate and publish contact information for a Title IX Coordinator responsible for overseeing Title IX compliance and grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble discusses duties of coordinators, dissemination of contact information, and importance for accessibility to complainants and respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of Non-Discrimination Policy (§106.8(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must disseminate their non-discrimination policy and contact information for Title IX coordination to students, employees, and applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments address publication venues, subjectivity concerns in publications implying discrimination, and consistency with other notification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption and Publication of Grievance Procedures (§106.8(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must adopt and publish grievance procedures that comply with §106.45 and make them accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble discusses expectations for publication, clarity, and ensuring procedures are current and understandable to community members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Outside the United States (§106.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules explain the application of Title IX procedures to off-campus programs and activities and considerations for conduct occurring outside the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document discusses consistency with federal law, impact on study-abroad participants, and constitutional considerations for extraterritorial application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational Institutions Controlled by Religious Organizations (§106.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients controlled by religious organizations may claim religious exemptions as provided under the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble discusses process and limitations for claiming religious exemptions and the interplay with Title IX obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactions with Other Legal Protections (First Amendment, Due Process, FERPA, Title VII, Clery Act, ADA/504/IDEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations clarify how Title IX obligations intersect with other constitutional and statutory protections, including free speech, due process rights, FERPA privacy rules, Title VII application to employees, and federal crime reporting obligations (Clery Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive discussion addresses potential conflicts, preemptive effect, required accommodations under disability law, and how recipients should navigate concurrent legal obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaliation Prohibited (§106.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: No recipient or other person may intimidate, threaten, coerce, or discriminate against any individual for exercising rights under Title IX or participating in Title IX processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble highlights enforcement, examples of prohibited retaliation, and the need for recipients to guard against retaliatory acts in their policies and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Requirements for Coordinators, Investigators, Decision-Makers
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and hearing officers must receive training on relevant legal standards, trauma-informed practices, relevance determinations, and evidence handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule points to mandatory training topics, concerns about bias and impartiality, directed questions about training content, and the need for ongoing education to ensure fair investigations and hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Disclosure to Department During Investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may be required to disclose records to the Department during Title IX investigations, consistent with other laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preemption, FERPA, and other privacy law interactions are discussed; recipients should be aware of obligations to permit Department access to records for compliance determinations.
